title: Isotropy makes logical circles round: the pinwheel law
claim: Isotropy makes logical circles round. (1) Isotropy principle: if a compact space of plane tilings with finite local complexity up to rigid motions is invariant under rotations and uniquely ergodic under translations, then for any rigid-motion-covariant metric on edges with c|x - y| - C <= D <= C|x - y| + C, D(e(0), e(nu))/n tends, for almost every tiling and every direction u, to one constant mu > 0. (2) Conditional on Radin's theorems (unique ergodicity under translations, complete rotational symmetry, recognizability), the bond distances of the pinwheel's parity laws (knots at tile corners; knots on tiles) satisfy (1): their circles are exactly round, a distance that counts distinctions and uses no lengths. (3) The same 1:2 triangle cut frame-consistently into the same five copies keeps one frame (four orientations); the 1:1 right triangle halved by its altitude gives the periodic tetrakis triangulation, whose parity laws have polygonal circles, an octagon with pi = 10/3 (knots at corners) and a square with pi = 4 (knots on tiles); roundness needs both an irrational angle (arctan(1/2), by Niven) and children of both handednesses. (4) A disc of radius R in a pinwheel tiling meets O(log R) tile orientations, so the roundness is exact only as a large-scale trend.
failure_conditions: A rotation-invariant, uniquely ergodic tiling space with linear bounds whose covariant bond distance has two different limits in two directions.
A pinwheel tiling level at which the number of tile orientations does not grow, or a consistent-cut level with more than one frame.
An even level of the 1:1 substitution that is not the checkerboard-diagonal (tetrakis) triangulation.
foundation_claim_scope: Tiling spaces with finite local complexity up to rigid motions (item 1); the Conway-Radin pinwheel (items 2 and 4); the frame-consistent cut of the 1:2 triangle and the 1:1 triangle's substitution (item 3).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs of Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and Propositions 3-4, conditional on Radin's cited theorems; check.py (57 s) verifies the substitutions in integer arithmetic, orientation counts per level, handedness, the 1:1 pattern at levels 2-14, the vertex-cycle lemma at 2137 vertices, the bounds on 40 exact least cycles and the orientations in discs, with four rejected controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: Radin and Sadun (1996) proved that shortest edge paths in pinwheel tilings, measured by Euclidean length, have length R + o(R); Radin (1993, 1994) proved unique ergodicity under translations and complete rotational symmetry; isotropy arguments for random tessellations are classical (Vahidi-Asl and Wierman). The delta is that bond distance, a count of distinctions with no lengths, is round, by an isotropy principle that covers every rigid-motion-covariant law, with the frame-consistent and 1:1 cuts as controls and the O(log R) orientation count.
